title: Impersonal se: what was decided and what was possible

sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know impersonal *se* from B1 Unit 6 (*se vive bien aquí*, *se puede entrar*): *se* + a third-person singular verb, with no subject. It is the way to say what was decided, needed or allowed without saying who did it.

sections.title: Se + singular verb
rows: Se decidió separar la Iglesia y el Estado.
*se decidió* + infinitive: it was decided to
Se necesitaba ser católico para ser ciudadano.
*se necesitaba* + infinitive: it was necessary to
Se podía registrar un matrimonio sin la Iglesia.
*se podía* + infinitive: it was possible to

items.spanish: En México se decidió separar la Iglesia y el Estado.
items.english: In Mexico it was decided to separate the Church and the State.

items.spanish: En Ecuador se necesitaba ser católico para ser ciudadano.
items.english: In Ecuador it was necessary to be Catholic to be a citizen.

items.spanish: Desde entonces se podía registrar un matrimonio sin pasar por la Iglesia.
items.english: From then on it was possible to register a marriage without going through the Church.

items.spanish: Se discutía mucho en los periódicos.
items.english: There was a lot of discussion in the newspapers.

sections.content: Impersonal *se* uses the singular verb, even before a plural place or group: *se discutía en los congresos*. With an infinitive, the verb stays singular: *se decidió separar*, not *se decidieron separar*. Compare *se crearon leyes* (passive with *se*, where the verb agrees with *leyes*).
